runs.text: Four thousand kilometres. Under one hour on the ground. June twenty seven, one thousand nine hundred and seventy six. Air France flight one hundred and thirty nine, from Tel Aviv to Paris, is hijacked after a stop in Athens. The hijackers, from the PFLP, the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine, and German radicals, fly it to Entebbe, Uganda. There they split the passengers. Israelis and Jews on one side. The others are set free. The French captain, Michel Bacos, is told he can go. He refuses. His whole crew stays. July three. Four Israeli Hercules planes fly four thousand kilometres south. They land at night. Within an hour, the hostages are free. Over a hundred hostages, flown home. Three hostages were killed. So was the commander, Yoni Netanyahu. Would your country fly four thousand kilometres for you? Tell me below. Because that's how far they flew.
